questions.question: Which of the following was ***not*** a part of the Constituent Assembly responsible for the formation of the Indian Constitution?

• The Constituent Assembly formally approved the draft **Constitution on 26 November 1949.**

**Jawaharlal Nehru**

**Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**

questions.question: After the Peshwas victory over Shivaji, the capital of Maratha kingdom became ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Poona**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• After the **death of Chhatrapati Shivaji in 1680**, the Maratha kingdom struggled to hold its own against the Mughals. 
 
• Shivaji’s sons, **Sambhaji was killed by the Mughals in 1689.**
 
• Sambhaji’s son **Shahu was a prisoner in the Mughal camps** of Malwa for almost eighteen years before his release in 1708. 
 
• Even though **Shahu did ascend the throne in 1708**, from 1713 onwards, it was the **Peshwa, Balaji Vishwanath who came to hold the reins of power.**
 
• **Till 1761**, when the Marathas were defeated at the hands of the Afghan marauder, Ahmad Shah Abdali, in the **Third Battle of Panipat**, **Peshwas exercised power on the Chattrapati’s behalf. **
 
• **The Chhatrapatis who followed Shahu** were reduced to being nominal heads and **retired to Satara.**
 
• The **Peshwas held fort at Pune** which came to be the real center of power. **So, option 4 is correct.**
 
• The Peshwas were assisted in their military endeavors by various Maratha chiefs — **Holkar, Scindia (Shinde), Gaekwad, and Bhonsle** — who led roving bands of soldiers that aided the Peshwa army.

questions.question: Which of the following process helps in absorption of water and minerals from Roots to Leaves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Transpiration__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f1c944588dff7ed66b6b6cfcf334bf304849adc53aad282e7ed498dc102e74e.png] 

 
• Transpiration is a process in which loss of water vapor takes place from plants leave through the help of stomata. 
 
• It is a physical process that is under the control of both external physical and physiological factors. 
 
• Transpiration requires solar radiation for energy which is absorbed by plants. 
 
• The rate of transpiration is proportional to the gradient in water vapor concentration between sources of water within the plant and the bulk atmosphere and the total resistance to water vapor diffusion of the plant.
 
• Plant loss water from leaves and stomata largely control leaf transpiration
 
• 
 
Regulation of stomatal aperture is very complex, as stomata respond to a variety of environmental (e.g., light, humidity, temperature, CO2 concentration) and endogenous (e.g., root and leaf hormone production and release, age) influences.

 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff1ed6fc970094d35c9abdf52ce2c2c30d160c647b2f2f2427adeae9d1c6ce95.png] 

 

 
• Sedimentation is the process of deposition of a solid particle from a state of suspension or solution in a fluid with the help of gravity. The particles that settle out from the solution become sediment, and in water treatment is known as sludge.
 
• Condensation is the change of water from its gaseous form (water vapor) into liquid water. It takes place in two ways: Either the air is cooled to its dew point or it becomes so saturated with water vapor that it cannot hold any more water.
 
• Accumulation is the process of water collecting in rivers, lakes, streams, oceans and other bodies of water. When water condenses and precipitates, it eventually runs off of surfaces and collects again in bodies of water. From there, the water evaporates, and the cycle begins again. Accumulation is important for a number of reasons, both in ecosystems and for humans.

• The organisms that can survive in the absence of air are called anaerobes. Through the anaerobic respiration process, they get the energy to survive. In the absence of oxygen, glucose breaks down into alcohol and carbon dioxide.
 
• When there is a temporary deficiency of oxygen, Our muscle cells respire anaerobically for a short period of time. questions.question: In which part of India, Dry soil is found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Rajasthan__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] 

 
• The soil and vegetation of Rajasthan vary with its wide-ranging topography of the state and the availability of water. There is a large variety of soils available in Rajasthan that are sandy, saline, alkaline and chalky (calcareous). 
 
• Clay, loamy, black lava soil and nitrogenous soils are also found in some parts of Rajasthan.
 
• The soil found in the Western Desert Regions has alkaline and saline soils with a calcareous base. There is some nitrate concentration in the soil of these regions. In these arid regions land is dry but not infertile.
 
• Wheat and mustard and bajra are grown in the western desert region.
 
• Due to limited rainfall, seasonal vegetation such as a few grass species, shrubs, and dwarf trees can be found. 
 
• The hilly tracts of the Aravali are characterized by the black, lava soils that sustain the growth of cotton and sugarcane.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87c1a28e731fadd9279228c1cea2f8e988a3f790bf9ccc89c9b0f02c423b1609.png] 

 

 
• Rajasthan is located in the northwestern part of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Its capital is Jaipur, known as Pink City.
 
• The Thar Desert or the Great Indian Desert is located in the landmass of Rajasthan.
 
• The Aravalli Range is located in Rajasthan and Guru Peak on Mount Abu is the highest peak in the Aravalli Range.
 
• Ranthambore National Park, Sariska National Park and Keoladeo park are located in Rajasthan.

questions.question: According to the law of demand, if all other items remain the same, then the relation between demand for goods and its value is?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Negative__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d75abffb1d7f21a0cb21fc40907655c03b3b6a401e1a3b03d94c609e009dc398.png] 

 
• The law of demand states that, if all other factors remain equal, the price of a good will be higher, the demand for that good will be less by people. 
 
• In other words, the higher the price, the lower the quantity demanded. 
 
• The amount of a good that buyers purchase at a higher price is less because as the price of a good goes up, so does the opportunity cost of buying that good. As a result, people will naturally avoid buying a product that will force them to forgo the consumption of something else they value more. 
 
• The law of demand is an economic principle that explains the negative correlation between the price of a good or service and its demand. 
 
• If all other factors remain the same, when the price of a good or service increases, the quantity of demand decreases, and vice versa.
 
• When all other things remain constant, there is an inverse relationship, or negative correlation, between price and the demand for goods and services. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a6a8f06b262806456af665e1b8217ceb8113d6bb49456f9395913c6248cabbdd.png] 

 
• A demand schedule is a table that shows the quantity demanded at each price.
 
• A demand curve is a graph that shows the quantity demanded at each price. Sometimes the demand curve is also called a demand schedule because it is a graphical representation of the demand scheduls.

questions.question: Indra Sawhney and others vs UOI case is related to?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reservation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e8eb9bb679eedf2fb873b59b31494e3eadcbcae26fe76a1ea53721b18ee81afd.png] 

**Indra Sawhney v. Union of India 1992:**

 
• At the beginning of the 1990s, the central government **implemented the Mandal Commission recommendations** for reservation of other backward classes.
 
• This created chaos in various sections of the society.
 
• Consequently, a PIL was filed, and resulted in one of the most significant judgments namely “**Indra Sawhney case”. **
 
• Also known as Mandal Case.
 
• Became **the cornerstone in the present reservation structure of the country. So, option 2 is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a6a8f06b262806456af665e1b8217ceb8113d6bb49456f9395913c6248cabbdd.png] 

**Salient features of Indra Sawhney judgment:**

 
• It **recognized socially and economically backward classes** as a category and recognized the** validity of the 27 percent reservation**.
 
• The **concept of the ‘creamy layer’ gained currency** through this judgment.
 
• Those among the OBCs who had transcended their social backwardness were to be excluded from the reservation.
 
• It laid down **a 50 percent limit on reservations** and observed that economic, social, and educational criteria were needed to define backward classes.
 
• **Reservation for backward classes** (which include OBCs and SCs & STs) should be **confined to initial appointments and not extend to promotions.**

questions.question: Which Indian Economist was awarded with prestigious Bodley medal on 15th March 2019?

• The Medal is awarded to individuals who have made outstanding contributions to the fields in which the Bodleian is active, including literature, culture, science and communication.
 
• Past winners of the honour include physicist Stephen Hawking, novelist Hilary Mantel and inventor of the World Wide Web Tim Berners-Lee.

• He is currently Thomas W. Lamont University Professor and Professor of Economics and Philosophy at Harvard University.
 
• He is an Indian economist who was awarded the 1998 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for his contributions to welfare economics and social choice theory and for his interest in the problems of society’s poorest members.
 
• Amartya Sen’s awards include Bharat Ratna (India) in 1999.
 
• He has been awarded with Friedenspreis des Deutschen Buchhandels, 2020.
 
• Some of the famous books of Amritya sen are Collective Choice and Social Welfare (1970), Poverty and Famines: An Essay on Entitlement and Deprivation (1981), Development as Freedom (1999); Rationality and Freedom (2002),

questions.question: An Act passed by Parliament is enacted only after the approval of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Every bill after being passed by both houses of Parliament is presented to the President for approval(Article 111)**. There are three alternatives before the president 

 
 
• He may give **approval to the bill**.
 
• He may **withhold his approval for the bill**.
 
• He may r**eturn the bill for reconsideration of the house.**
 
• If the **bill is passed it becomes an act and is a place in the statute book.**
 
 
 
• President enjoys **suspensive veto, absolute veto, pocket veto**.
 
• Article **123 gives power to the President that he can issue ordinance when one of the houses of the Parliament is not in session. The maximum validity of an ordinance is 6 months and 6 weeks**. An ordinance will expire after 6 weeks once both houses of the Parliament are in session.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The President is the formal head of the executive, legislature and judiciary of India.
 
• He is the **first citizen of India(Article 53).** The idea of the **President is taken from United states of America.**
 
• He is the **commander-in-chief of the Indian Armed Forces.{Article 53(40}.**
 
• The election of President is done by **Single Electoral College,** which consists of the elected members of **both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of all the States and also of NCT of Delhi and the Union Territory of Puducherry. (Article 54)**
 
• The President shall hold office for a term of **5 years from the date on which he enters upon his office. (Article 56)**.
 
• The oath is taken by the President in the presence of the **Chief Justice of India.** 
 
• If the President violates the law of the Constitution, he may be removed from office by **impeachment (Article 61).**
 
• The President can hand over the **resign to Vice-President**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Under Article 58, a candidate should fulfill the following eligibility conditions to contest the election to the Office of President: -

 
 
• Must be a **citizen of India**,
 
• Must have **completed 35 years of age,**
 
• Must be **eligible to be a member of Lok Sabha.**
 
 
 
• **President has the power to reduce the punishment of a person or can change the nature of punishment(Article 72).**
 
• President has emergency power and they are of three types.:
 
 
• ** National Emergency (Article 352).**
 
• **President’s rule (Article 356 & 365).**
 
• **Financial Emergency(Article 360). **

questions.question: Hydrogen bomb is based on which Nuclear process?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thermal fusion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The hydrogen bomb is also known as the** Thermonuclear bomb or H-bomb.**
 
• **H**-bomb is a weapon whose **enormous explosive power results from an uncontrolled self-sustaining chain reaction in which isotopes of hydrogen combine under extremely high temperatures to form helium in a process known as nuclear fusion.**
 
• To make a hydrogen bomb, one would need **uranium or plutonium as well as two other isotopes of hydrogen, called deuterium and tritium.** The hydrogen bomb relies on f**usion, the process of taking two separate atoms and putting them together to form a third atom.**
 
• The way the hydrogen bomb works — it’s really a combination of **fission and fusion together**.
 
• In both cases, a significant amount of energy is released, **which drives the explosion and more energy is released during the fusion process, which causes a bigger blast.**
 
• The most common bomb design that employs these features is called the **Teller-Ulam configuration**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An H-bomb is a three-stage weapon: fission, fusion, and then fission again.
 
• **First, the stages of the weapon are separated into a triggering. **The energy released at this stage is mainly due to **nuclear fission -- because the atoms of plutonium are split. **Tritium is often added to the center of the plutonium core to "**boost" the fission explosion with some additional fusion energy.** Heated the material in the central column to **100 million degrees celsius so that a much more powerful fusion reaction** can be started there.
 
• ​The main fusion reaction involves concentrated **deuterium and tritium (**both heavy isotopes of hydrogen) -- which become spontaneously available when neutrons from the first stage explosion bombard a solid material called **"lithium deuteride" located in the central column. When this hydrogen-rich mix is heated to 100 million degrees, the deuterium and tritium atoms "fuse" together, releasing enormous amounts of energy. This is the "H" or "thermonuclear" part of the bomb.**
 
• The fusion reaction gives off an incredible burst of **extremely powerful neutrons -- so powerful that they can split or "fission" atoms of uranium-238 (called "depleted uranium") **-- which is impossible at lower energy levels. **This third stage more than doubles the power of the explosion and produces most of the radioactive fallout from the weapon.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/157b5c8d81eb1de7eac710fd84fc15e62204974a5cdc124243f408f95e705595.png]

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Michel Phelps.**

• Michael Phelps is an **American swimmer who holds the record for most Olympics medals**.
 
• He was the first **American male swimmer** to earn a spot on five Olympic teams and also made history as the oldest individual gold medalist in Olympic swimming history at the age of 28.

questions.question: Which is the world's highest plateau?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tibetan Plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Tibetan Plateau is the **highest and biggest plateau on Earth**,
 
• It is popularly known as the **roof of the world.** It is located in **southwestern China.**
 
• It has resulted from a **collision between two tectonic plates about 55 million years ago**.
 
• Other names of this plateau are **Plateau of Tibet, Chinese (Pinyin) Qingzang Gaoyuan or (Wade-Giles romanization) Ch’ing-Tsang Kao-yuan, also called Tibetan Highlands or Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The plateau, which has an area of about **965,000 square miles (2,500,000 square km), is a region of tangled mountains and uplands that are generally above 13,000 to 15,000 feet (4,000 to 5,000 meters) in elevation**. 
 
• **Mount Everest (Qomolangma Feng), rising 29,035 feet (8,850 meters) above sea level on the China-Nepal border, is the world’s highest peak of the world.**
 
• Several rivers start from this plateau and flow eastwards and southwards.
 
• The eastwards flowing rivers are the **Yellow River, Yangtze, and the Mekong**.
 
• The southward flowing ones include the **Salween, the Indus River in India, and the Irrawaddy River in Burma.**

questions.question: Nuclear fusion reaction is based on which of the following equation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nuclear Fusion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d75abffb1d7f21a0cb21fc40907655c03b3b6a401e1a3b03d94c609e009dc398.png] 

 
• Nuclear fusion is the process in which two light nuclei fuse or join together to form a larger nucleus.
 
• During this process, some of the mass of the fusing nuclei is converted to energy which is released. 
 
• Fusion is the process that powers active stars, releasing large quantities of energy.
 
• The origin of the energy released in the fusion of light elements is due to an interplay of two opposing forces: the nuclear force that draws together protons and neutrons and the Coulomb force that causes protons to repel each other. 
 
• The protons are positively charged and repel each other, but they nonetheless stick together, demonstrating the existence of another force referred to as nuclear attraction. This force, called the strong nuclear force, overcomes electric repulsion in a very close range.
 
• The difference in mass is released as energy according to Albert Einstein’s mass-energy equivalence formula

 E =mc2 . 

 
• If the input nuclei are sufficiently massive, the resulting fusion product will be heavier than the sum of the reactants’ original masses, in which case the reaction requires an external source of energy.
 
• The dividing line between “light” and “heavy” is iron-56. Above this atomic mass, energy will generally be released by nuclear fission reactions; below this mass, energy will be released by fusion.

questions.question: Which of the following given options is not the type of Fiscal bill presented by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __728 days__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d75abffb1d7f21a0cb21fc40907655c03b3b6a401e1a3b03d94c609e009dc398.png] 

 
• Treasury bills are issued when the government needs money for a short period.
 
• Funds collected through such tools are typically used to meet the short term requirements of the government, hence, to reduce the overall fiscal deficit of a country.
 
• These bills are money market instruments issued only by the central government, and the interest on them is determined by the market forces.
 
• Treasury bills have a maximum tenure of 364 days. 
 
• At present, treasury bills are issued in three maturities — 91-day, 182-day and 364-day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a6a8f06b262806456af665e1b8217ceb8113d6bb49456f9395913c6248cabbdd.png] 

 
• In 1997 the government also issued 14-day immediate treasury bills.
 
• Treasury bills were first issued in India in 1917. They are issued via auctions conducted by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) at regular intervals.
 
• Banks give treasury bills to the RBI to get money under repo. Similarly, they can also keep it to fulfill their Statutory Liquid Ratio (SLR) requirements.
 
• Treasury bills have an advantage over other market instruments because of the zero-risk weightage associated with them. 
 
• The secondary market of T-Bills is very active and they have a higher degree of tradability.
